decisions.summary: A mon price beside a silver-monme wage states both units; the copper-to-silver rate is not researched here and is listed as still open in the answer.
decisions.why: The request asks for each price 'with the same period's day-laborer wage' and for 'what is still open'; it does not ask for a unified unit or a conversion (the skill converts). Reporting a monme wage in monme is reporting the wage; researching the exchange rate would be a fifth question beyond the four approved. The plan cites 'the spec, User Story 2' for this, but US2 is not in the bundle, so this ruling rests on the request alone.

decisions.summary: Where no source gives the unskilled day wage of the same place and period, the question records that wage as SILENT.
decisions.why: SILENT is the request's own verdict vocabulary. The standard is 'where a source gives one': SILENT must come from the question's own search, not from the 'Wages in hand' inventory, which is only what the passes happened to carry.

decisions.summary: When the same-place/period unskilled wage is SILENT, the nearest unskilled wage of another place or period is named with its place, unit and gap in years.
decisions.why: Reporting a wage no source gives is physically impossible; the substitute is disclosed as a substitute (place, unit, gap), so the reader can see it is not the same place and period, and the request's purpose (laborer-day conversion) is served as far as the sources allow.

decisions.summary: A craftsman's wage is used where no unskilled wage exists, named as 'the nearest wage' with its place, unit and gap in years.
decisions.why: The request fixes exactly one attribute of the wage - 'unskilled' - because the skill converts by unskilled laborer-days (~13 sen). The block commits the substitute to carrying its place, unit and gap, but not its class; as written a craftsman's wage can stand beside a price as 'the nearest wage' and be read as the laborer-day denominator, which defeats the request's stated purpose. Legitimate once the block says the substitute's class (unskilled / craftsman) is named alongside its place, unit and gap, and that a craftsman's wage is never presented as the unskilled wage.

decisions.summary: Four new questions, subject=money, no drawing page, level counts-and-measurements, setting tags, coverage table; project-computed figures labeled as the project's arithmetic.
decisions.why: FR-001/FR-002 and the four request questions, China as comparison (Qing silence, Qing mule). The table does not name the cart, porters separately from the pack horse, the used kimono, sewing, silk bedding, or the brewer's price; they are carried only by 'every attested figure, every silence', which is what keeps D1 within - each must appear as a figure or a SILENT verdict. Labeling project arithmetic serves the request's ATTESTED/NOT ATTESTED distinction.

decisions.id: Technical Context: wage beside each figure; SILENT fallback to the nearest wage with class, place, unit and gap; craftsman's wage only where no unskilled exists, always named as a craftsman's and never shown as the unskilled wage
decisions.summary: Each price sits beside the same place and period's unskilled day wage where a source gives one; where none does the wage is reported SILENT and the nearest wage is named with its class, place, unit and gap in years.
decisions.why: The request asks for the unskilled day wage of the same place and period. Where no source gives that wage, meeting the rule is physically impossible, and the request's own verdict vocabulary includes SILENT. The fallback adds a labeled nearest wage; it does not replace the requested one. The changed text strengthens fidelity: a craftsman's wage is named by its class and is never presented as the unskilled wage the skill converts by, so the request's purpose (laborer-day conversion) is not corrupted.

decisions.id: Technical Context: copper-to-silver rate left open
decisions.summary: Mon prices beside silver-monme wages state both units; the exchange rate is not written and the answer lists it as still open.
decisions.why: The figures the request asks for (price in mon, with the same period's wage) are still delivered, both units stated. The request's 'what is still open' clause provides for the missing rate, and the skill does the conversion. No figure is withheld and no conversion is invented.
